# The product supervises the human's attention, not the agents

> This is client work: the decisions are the user's because the responsibility is, and an autonomous supervisor moves risk somewhere nobody looks.

Applies to `crates/**`, `app/**`, `web/**`.

<!-- archwarden:yours -->

## Context

_Everything between these two markers is yours. archwarden never rewrites it._

<!-- archwarden:end -->

## Considered and rejected

- **Supervisor–worker orchestration** (nothing refuses it) — The dominant pattern in every agent framework, and what the comparable tools build. It removes the human from decisions the human wants to make.
- **L3 autonomy, agents deciding for themselves** (nothing refuses it) — The goal was never to decide less. It was to decide better, which is the opposite optimisation.
- **Parallel panes with no supervision** (nothing refuses it) — Keeps the human in the loop and helps them not at all. Prettier terminals, same cognitive load.

## What keeps it

Nothing can. It is a claim about what the product is for. No import boundary can tell a queue that ranks decisions from one that takes them.
